label: sec:q-gl-conjecture-intro
html:
The failure of the quantum differential to square to zero organises this section. The obstruction it measures is what confines the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence to the non-torsion locus: the correspondence is well-defined only where that obstruction is controlled, and each result below either quantifies the obstruction or works within that locus. The construction is abstract, but the next section makes it concrete by instantiating the correspondence as q-opers.

We open with the Definition: q-Langlands dual group, the deformation of the classical dual that carries the substrate parameter on the spectral side. The Conjecture: q-Geometric Langlands correspondence then states the equivalence itself — between q-\mathcal{D}-modules on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q} and quasi-coherent sheaves on \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}, well-defined on the non-torsion locus. The Proposition: Obstruction to q-flatness and its proof calibrate the conjecture: they compute the Yekutieli obstruction classes and exhibit them as the precise substrate-theoretic measure of the failure of d_q^2 = 0.

The section closes with two structural conjectures organised by this obstruction. The Conjecture: Kummer filtration on q-local systems reads the Kummer reduction as the level-n lifting obstruction of q-local systems through the brane tower, pinning the correspondence to the arithmetic locus where the quantum integer [n]_q is nonzero. The Conjecture: Fibre-functor mediation of the q-Langlands correspondence asserts that the rigid fibre functor implements the equivalence by Tannaka–Krein reconstruction, with the Remark: Proof sketch for fibre-functor mediation outlining the argument the next section instantiates concretely for q-opers.
